summary: Sichuan spicy cauliflower: a 700-gram head of cauliflower cooked sous vide at 85°C for about 40 minutes with chili oil, crushed Sichuan peppercorn, garlic and ginger, or microwaved and then stir-fried; good hot or cold, like a spicy pickle.
glance: 1 head, about 700 grams, halved or in florets
1 tablespoon crushed Sichuan peppercorn (feel free to double)
microwave the florets until partly tender, then about 5 minutes in a hot skillet (untested)

summary: Roasted asparagus on a pistachio puree: 2 cups of roasted pistachios blended with lemon, garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, olive oil and water into a creamy nut spread, with asparagus roasted at 400°F for about 10 minutes and blistered under the broiler.
glance: makes more than one bunch needs; also good with raw endive or roasted cauliflower
balsamic, chopped pistachios, Maldon salt, tarragon
faq: What is a nut puree like Matt Dillon's?

At Sitka and Spruce and Bar Sajor, Matt Dillon serves salads and small plates on bases of nut purees that eat more like a nut-based hummus: rich, creamy, slightly fluffy, and packed with the flavor of roasted nuts.
How do you make pistachio puree?

Blend unsalted roasted pistachios with lemon juice, garlic, salt, cumin, smoked paprika and half the olive oil, then with the blender running on medium-low drizzle in the rest of the oil and the water until the color lightens and it's fairly smooth but not textureless. Press plastic wrap on the surface to prevent oxidation.
Can I use a food processor?
The author suspects so, and also suspects you could put everything in at once and use less oil.
Can I change the flavors?
Yes, e.g. orange juice and zest with ras el hanout, but don't overpower the pistachio flavor: the pistachios should be the stars.
How do you roast the asparagus?
Toss with olive oil and kosher salt and roast at 400°F until tender, about 10 minutes, then use the broiler or a blowtorch until blackened in spots.
What else can I use the puree on?
It would go equally great with raw endive or roasted cauliflower. The recipe makes more than one bunch of asparagus needs, about the smallest amount you can easily make in a blender.

summary: Improved sesame corn muffins, not too sweet: toasted sesame seeds, medium-grind cornmeal, buttermilk and a little toasted sesame oil, mixed just until moistened and baked at 375°F for 20 to 25 minutes; makes 12.
glance: 1/2 cup + 2 tablespoons hulled seeds, 1/2 cup toasted first
faq: What changed in the improved version?

Pre-toasting the sesame seeds, using buttermilk instead of buttermilk powder, changing the ratio of cornmeal to all-purpose flour and upping the salt all contribute to a better structure and more flavor.
Are these muffins sweet?
Not particularly. Serve them with plenty of room-temperature butter and honey as a breakfast treat, or go savory and serve them instead of cornbread with a big bowl of vegetarian chili.
How do I keep the muffins tender?
Do not overmix. Just moisten the flour; some small lumps are fine, since overmixing makes tough muffins.
How do I know they're done?
They are lightly golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, after 20 to 25 minutes. Don't overbake. Cool 5 minutes in the pan and 5 more on a rack.
What can I add?
Blueberries, grated ginger, or lemon or orange zest.

summary: Mexican matzo brei, or Jewish chilaquiles: a thick "handmade" corn tortilla torn and fried in canola oil until a little crispy but still chewy, then scrambled with 2 eggs, cheddar and hot sauce; a single serving.
glance: 1 thick Trader Joe's "handmade" corn tortilla, torn small
a few minutes, until a little crispy but still chewy, then add the eggs
faq: What is matzo brei?

A classic Jewish egg dish, often eaten during Passover when leavened bread is forbidden. Matza can also be spelled matzo, matzoh or matzah, and everyone has their own technique: soaking in water or in the egg, breaking it up large or small, frying it as a cake or scrambling it.
What are chilaquiles?
A classic Mexican dish in which corn tortillas are fried up crispy with scrambled eggs, with everyone having a style with different cheeses, sauces and chilis.
Why combine them?
Thicker "handmade" corn tortillas don't easily fry crispy but develop a tender texture that reminded the author of matzo brei, and it was absolutely delicious.
How do you make it?

Heat a non-stick skillet over high heat with 1 tablespoon of canola oil, add the torn tortilla and fry for a few minutes, shaking occasionally. Add the eggs, salt and pepper and cook like scrambled eggs, adding the cheddar when the eggs are almost done.
What do I serve it with?
Your favorite hot sauce; the author has been enjoying Bullard's Louisiana Habanero.

summary: Fresh pappardelle with cauliflower and zucchini: cauliflower and zucchini gently sauteed in butter with roasted garlic and a pinch of tarragon, timed to finish with the pasta, which cooks about 3 minutes, then topped with shaved pecorino romano.
glance: 1 pound fresh pappardelle, about 3 minutes to al dente
2 heads roasted at 400°F for about 40 minutes, or 1-2 minced cloves
faq: What makes a simple pasta like this great?

Choosing good ingredients and getting the timing right. Use beautiful ingredients, time the vegetables and pasta to finish at the same moment, and check the seasoning carefully; sad pasta and overcooked vegetables won't do.
Why roast the garlic?
The author wanted a mild, sweet flavor and didn't even caramelize the vegetables. If you don't have time, skip roasting and add a minced clove or two to the saute.
How do I roast the garlic?
Trim the upper 1/4 inch off each head, rub with olive oil, wrap in foil and roast at 400°F for about 40 minutes, until easily pierced with a fork.
What cheese goes on it?
Thin shavings of pecorino romano cut with a vegetable peeler. A nice big spoonful of ricotta, such as Calabro, also works.
How do I time the dish?
When the vegetables are 3 minutes from done, usually just after adding the zucchini, turn them to low and drop the fresh noodles into the boiling water.

summary: Avocado-tomatillo salsa, a thicker taqueria-style avocado sauce: tomatillos, garlic, jalapeno and shallot dry-roasted about 5 minutes until blackened in spots, then blended with avocado, lime juice, cilantro, cumin and salt.
glance: dry-roast about 5 minutes, until many black spots

summary: Five-minute Indian-style cabbage: black mustard seeds popped in hot oil, a few quick spices stirred in off the heat, then sliced green cabbage stir-fried on maximum heat about 1 minute for crisp-tender or 2-3 minutes for tender.
faq: Why mustard seeds with cabbage?
Everything in the cabbage family goes great with mustard, so mustard seeds are the primary flavoring. Mustard oil, used in place of the vegetable oil, intensifies the mustard flavor.
How do I temper the mustard seeds without burning them?

Heat the oil over medium-high heat, wait 10 seconds, add the mustard seeds, and as soon as they pop pull the skillet off the heat and add the cumin, turmeric and cayenne, stirring 10 more seconds. Have everything chopped and measured in advance.
How long do I cook the cabbage?
Add the cabbage and salt, return to the heat and raise it to maximum, stir-frying until crisp-tender (about 1 minute) or tender (about 2-3 minutes).
What optional additions work?
Garlic, ginger, unsweetened shredded coconut, fresh chiles or chile flakes, garam masala, with cilantro and/or lemon juice to garnish.
Is it vegan?
Use vegetable oil rather than ghee for the vegan option; it is gluten-free.

summary: Eggplant in a mild, aromatic kaffir-lime coconut curry: scored Japanese eggplants roasted at 450°F for at least 30 minutes, served on a fresh paste of kaffir lime leaf, lemongrass, garlic, ginger and Thai basil fried 1 minute and stirred into coconut milk off the heat.
glance: 4 as part of a rice-based meal
450°F, at least 30 minutes, until completely tender and browning
fry 1 minute, then stir in the coconut milk off the heat
yield: 4 as part of a rice-based meal
faq: What does kaffir lime taste like?
It has a clean, high-note citrus flavor without any actual acidity, almost like essential oil of lime. The risk of using too much is a sauce that tastes like Pledge, the lemon furniture polish.
What if I can't find kaffir lime?
Use 2 teaspoons of lime zest, though the author says it won't be the same.
Why not simmer the coconut milk?
If coconut-milk sauces simmer and reduce for long, they can develop an unpleasant gelatinous texture. Here the coconut milk is simply stirred into the fried curry paste off the heat.
How do I prepare the eggplant?

Slice the long Japanese eggplants lengthwise, score deeply on the diagonal into diamonds without cutting all the way through, brush with oil, season with salt and roast on a baking sheet at 450°F (convection if possible).
How is this different from a Thai green curry?
It has some but not all of the same ingredients, and you don't get the green color in the sauce, but you do get distinct, bright flavors. It was planned to be mild but very aromatic.

summary: Rigatoni with roasted cauliflower and a spicy tomato-cream sauce spiked with vodka: cauliflower roasted at 450°F for at least 20 minutes, a blended fire-roasted tomato sauce simmered with the pasta for the last minute, and green olives and ricotta salata; serves 4.
glance: 450°F for at least 20 minutes, until browned in many spots
two 14.5-ounce cans crushed tomatoes (fire-roasted), 3/4 cup cream, 2 tablespoons vodka
faq: What dishes inspired this pasta?
A cross between Penne alla Vodka (the tomato-cream sauce spiked with a bit of vodka) and Pasta alla Norma, with cauliflower instead of eggplant.
How do you roast the cauliflower?
Toss florets with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and salt and roast at 450°F, tossing occasionally, until completely tender and browned in many spots, at least 20 minutes.
How do I add smoky flavor?
Use fire-roasted crushed tomatoes such as Muir Glen, and for even more smoke add 1/2 teaspoon of smoked paprika to the sauce.
Why finish the pasta in the sauce?
Cooking the pasta with the sauce for the last minute or so helps the sauce cling to it. Reserve a cup of the pasta water and use some to thin the sauce if it's too thick.
What cheese goes on top?
Thin shavings of ricotta salata. If you can't find it, a young pecorino or something semi-soft and salty would work.

summary: Red lentil and kabocha squash soup with quick harissa oil, a sneak peek from the Herbivoracious cookbook: squash browned in olive oil, spiced, simmered with red lentils in 6 cups of water for about 30 minutes, pureed and drizzled with the oil.
glance: about 30 minutes, until the lentils mostly fall apart
cooking pumpkin, butternut or acorn squash for the kabocha
faq: Can I use other lentils?
No. Red lentils basically dissolve when cooked, leaving a silky smooth texture. Don't try this recipe with green or black lentils.
What if I don't have kabocha squash?

Use a cooking pumpkin (such as a sugar pie pumpkin) or butternut or acorn squash. You won't need a whole squash, so it's a good way to use leftovers; if the squash is already cooked, just heat it through in the first step.
Is the soup good for kids?
It is quite mild if you leave the harissa oil off their portions, and with the garnish the flavors come alive for everyone else.
What is harissa oil?

Oil infused with harissa, the classic North African spice paste, terrific for grilling vegetables, drizzling on soups, or spicing up a vinaigrette. The quick version warms olive oil with chile sauce, pepper flakes, cumin, caraway, coriander, sumac and garlic for about 5 minutes, rests 5 more, then is pureed and strained. It keeps a few days in the refrigerator.
How do I puree the soup safely?
Puree thoroughly with a blender or immersion blender, following the hot-soup safety tips in the cookbook.
